title: Is Checkatrade Worth It? vs MyBuilder and Bark (2026)
desc: Is Checkatrade worth it in 2026? What Checkatrade, MyBuilder and Bark really cost UK tradespeople per won job, how leads are shared, and what to do instead.

blocks.h1: Is Checkatrade worth it? *Checkatrade, MyBuilder and Bark compared.*
blocks.lede: Checkatrade can pay for itself if you do bigger jobs in a busy area and the badge wins you trust. MyBuilder and Bark are cheaper to start but every lead is shared, so the real cost sits in the jobs you lose. The only way to know is to work out what one won job costs you on each.

blocks.html:
Is Checkatrade worth it?

For some UK tradespeople, yes. The vetting badge carries weight with homeowners, and on large jobs like kitchens, bathrooms and extensions one win covers a lot of membership. For small jobs it rarely adds up, and the 12 month term means a bad decision costs you for a year.

MyBuilder and Bark work differently: no big monthly fee, but you pay each time you want to quote, and the same job is shown to several trades. Here is how they compare.

What Checkatrade, MyBuilder and Bark cost in 2026

PlatformHow you payReported costShared?
CheckatradeMonthly membership, usually 12 monthsFrom £30 + VAT (no leads at that tier); members report around £60 to £180 a month for plans with leads, depending on trade and areaVaries by plan
MyBuilderFee when a homeowner shortlists youAbout £2 to £35 per shortlist, depending on job sizeSeveral trades shortlisted
BarkCredits per lead£1.80 + VAT per credit; most leads roughly £7 to £40Up to about 5 professionals

Two details catch people out. Bark credits bought since November 2025 expire after three months. And on MyBuilder you pay for the chance to quote, not for the job, so a homeowner who goes quiet still costs you the fee.

The sum that tells you if it pays

Cost per won job = what you spent on the platform ÷ jobs you actually won from it.

Pay £20 a lead and win one in five, and each job cost £100. Win one in ten and it cost £200. On a £2,000 bathroom, £100 is fine. On a £90 call out, it is the whole job.

Do this for the last three to six months, platform by platform, and then compare each figure with your profit on a typical job. The platform that looks cheapest per lead is often not the cheapest per job.

Checkatrade vs MyBuilder vs Bark: which is better?

  • Checkatrade suits established trades doing larger jobs who value the badge and can commit for a year.
  • MyBuilder suits trades who want to pick jobs one at a time with no standing fee, and who are happy to compete on quotes.
  • Bark suits businesses that respond fast and quote cheaply on small jobs, but watch the credit expiry.

Whichever you choose, start with the option you can stop tomorrow, not a 12 month term.

What to build instead

  1. Google Business Profile. Free, and it is where most local customers look first. Our Google Business Profile checklist covers every setting.
  2. Google reviews you own. Reviews on a platform stay on the platform. Reviews on Google follow your business.
  3. Your own website. A page for each service and town, real photos and a tap to call button. See what a trade website needs.
  4. Referrals. Ask every happy customer, and stay in touch with past clients.

Getting the most from Checkatrade if you stay

  • Respond to every enquiry fast, by phone where possible. Speed matters most on shared leads.
  • Collect reviews on Checkatrade and Google. Your Checkatrade reviews stay on Checkatrade; Google reviews follow you whatever you decide next year.
  • Narrow your categories and areas so you only pay for work you want.
  • Track every job by source in a simple spreadsheet, so renewal is a decision based on numbers, not a feeling.
  • Diary the renewal date two months ahead, so you have time to decide.

What UK homeowners check besides the badge

A vetting badge helps, but homeowners also search your business name on Google, look at your reviews and photos, and check you look established. A trade with a strong Google profile and a clear website can win the same customers without paying for a directory listing. items.q: How much does Checkatrade cost per month?
items.a: The entry plan starts from £30 + VAT a month but does not include leads. Members commonly report paying around £60 to £180 a month for plans with leads, depending on trade and area.
It is free to join. You pay a fee, typically about £2 to £35, when a homeowner shortlists you, whether or not you win the job.

items.q: How much does a Bark lead cost?
items.a: Credits cost £1.80 + VAT and most leads need between about 5 and 20 credits, so roughly £7 to £40 a lead. Each lead can go to up to about five professionals.
Memberships are usually on a 12 month term. Check your agreement for the end date and notice period before you sign or renew.
For many trades, a complete Google Business Profile with steady reviews and a website of your own. They cost nothing per lead and the customers come to you alone.
